title: Acute Anterior STEMI with Cardiogenic Shock Risk
presentation: Severe retrosternal crushing chest pain for 45 minutes radiating to jaw and left shoulder, accompanied by diaphoresis, acute nausea, and marked dyspnea.
vitals: BP 90/60 mmHg, HR 48 bpm, RR 24/min, SpO2 93% on room air, Temp 36.8C
labs: ECG: 4mm ST-segment elevation in V2-V4 with reciprocal ST depression in II, III, aVF; High-sensitivity Troponin I: 4,850 ng/L (markedly elevated).
trueContraindications: Beta-blockers (Metoprolol/Atenolol) contraindicated due to severe bradycardia (HR 48 bpm) and borderline hypotension (BP 90/60 mmHg)
Nitrates (Nitroglycerin) contraindicated in acute hypotension and risk of right ventricular involvement

title: Non-ST Elevation Myocardial Infarction (NSTEMI) in Diabetic Patient
presentation: Intermittent sub-mammary burning chest discomfort over 6 hours, worsening with exertion, associated with diaphoresis and fatigue.
vitals: BP 148/92 mmHg, HR 86 bpm, RR 18/min, SpO2 97% on room air
labs: ECG: 2mm horizontal ST-depression in V4-V6 and T-wave inversion in I, aVL; Serial hs-cTnT: 320 ng/L rising to 780 ng/L; Fasting glucose: 182 mg/dL.
medications: Metformin 1000mg BD, Empagliflozin 10mg OD, Amlodipine 5mg OD

referenceDifferentials.condition: Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease with Esophageal Spasm

trueContraindications: Withhold Metformin prior to coronary angiography due to contrast-induced nephropathy risk

title: Acute Decompensated Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction
presentation: Progressive exertional breathlessness, orthopnea (3 pillows), paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, and bilateral lower limb edema over 10 days.
vitals: BP 168/98 mmHg, HR 96 bpm (irregular), RR 26/min, SpO2 90% on air, JVP +6 cm
labs: NT-proBNP: 3,400 pg/mL; Serum Creatinine: 1.4 mg/dL; Echocardiogram: LVEF 55%, grade II diastolic dysfunction, LA dilation.
medications: Ramipril 5mg OD, Indapamide 2.5mg OD, Bisoprolol 2.5mg OD
trueContraindications: Avoid initiation of non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers with negative inotropic effects in acute congestion
Avoid NSAIDs due to sodium retention and renal perfusion deterioration

title: Atrial Fibrillation with Rapid Ventricular Response (RVR)
presentation: Acute onset palpitations, lightheadedness, and mild dyspnea lasting 4 hours.
vitals: BP 112/74 mmHg, HR 148 bpm (irregularly irregular), RR 20/min, SpO2 96%
labs: ECG: Absent P waves, irregular R-R intervals, narrow QRS tachycardia at 145-155 bpm; Potassium: 4.1 mmol/L; TSH: 1.2 mIU/L.

referenceDifferentials.condition: Atrial Fibrillation with Rapid Ventricular Response

trueContraindications: Avoid immediate electrical cardioversion without prior transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) or >=3 weeks therapeutic anticoagulation unless hemodynamically unstable
Calculate CHA2DS2-VASc score prior to discharge

title: Acute Pericarditis with Pleuritic Chest Pain
presentation: Sharp retrosternal chest pain radiating to the left trapezius ridge, significantly aggravated by lying flat and deep inspiration, relieved by sitting forward.
vitals: BP 124/78 mmHg, HR 88 bpm, RR 16/min, SpO2 99%, Temp 37.6C
labs: ECG: Widespread concave ST elevation across leads I, II, aVF, V2-V6 with PR-segment depression in II and reciprocal PR elevation in aVR; CRP: 48 mg/L; hs-cTnI: normal.
trueContraindications: Avoid systemic corticosteroids as first-line therapy due to increased risk of pericarditis recurrence

title: Stanford Type A Aortic Dissection
presentation: Sudden onset catastrophic 'tearing' chest pain radiating directly to the interscapular back, accompanied by syncope.
vitals: BP right arm: 178/96 mmHg; BP left arm: 122/70 mmHg (asymmetric >20 mmHg); HR 92 bpm; RR 22/min
labs: CXR: Widened mediastinum (>8cm); D-dimer: 5,400 ng/mL; High-sensitivity troponin: mildly elevated.

referenceDifferentials.condition: Acute Stanford Type A Aortic Dissection

trueContraindications: ABSOLUTE CONTRAINDICATION to thrombolytics, therapeutic heparin, and antiplatelet loading doses
Immediate emergent cardiothoracic surgical consultation

title: Severe Symptomatic Aortic Stenosis
presentation: Exertional syncope while climbing stairs, progressive angina on walking 100 meters, and dyspnea NYHA class III.
vitals: BP 108/84 mmHg (narrow pulse pressure), HR 72 bpm (pulsus parvus et tardus), SpO2 95%
labs: Cardiac auscultation: Harsh crescendo-decrescendo systolic ejection murmur at right upper sternal border radiating to carotids with soft S2; Echo: Aortic valve area 0.65 cm2, mean gradient 48 mmHg, peak velocity 4.4 m/s.

referenceDifferentials.condition: Severe Symptomatic Calcific Aortic Valve Stenosis
Coronary Artery Disease with Exertional Angina

trueContraindications: Avoid aggressive vasodilators (Nitrates, ACE inhibitors, high-dose DHP-CCB) which can precipitate critical hypotension and circulatory collapse

title: Hypertrophic Obstructive Cardiomyopathy (HOCM) in Young Athlete
presentation: Recurrent near-syncope during intense football training, accompanied by atypical chest tightness and exertional breathlessness.
vitals: BP 120/75 mmHg, HR 68 bpm, SpO2 99%
labs: ECG: Deep voltage criteria for LVH, dagger-like narrow deep Q waves in inferolateral leads (II, III, aVF, V5-V6); Echo: Interventricular septal thickness 22mm, systolic anterior motion (SAM) of mitral valve with LVOT gradient 52 mmHg at rest.
trueContraindications: Avoid Digoxin, Nitrates, and pure vasodilators as they increase the LVOT gradient and worsen dynamic obstruction
Avoid intense competitive athletic participation pending electrophysiology risk stratification

title: Subacute Infective Endocarditis with Valvular Vegetation
presentation: 4 weeks of low-grade remittent fevers, night sweats, anorexia, 5kg unintended weight loss, and new petechial lesions on conjunctiva.
vitals: BP 128/68 mmHg, HR 92 bpm, RR 18/min, SpO2 96%, Temp 38.4C
labs: Blood cultures: 3/3 sets positive for Streptococcus viridans; Echo: 9mm mobile vegetation on aortic valve cusp with mild aortic regurgitation murmur; ESR: 86 mm/hr; Urinalysis: microscopic hematuria.
trueContraindications: Penicillin, Ampicillin, Ceftriaxone, and Cefazolin strictly contraindicated due to IgE-mediated anaphylaxis history. Prescribe IV Vancomycin plus Gentamicin

title: Third-Degree (Complete) Atrioventricular Block
presentation: Three discrete episodes of sudden syncope without prodrome (Adams-Stokes attacks) over 48 hours, profound fatigue.
vitals: BP 164/58 mmHg, HR 32 bpm (regular, slow), RR 16/min, SpO2 96%
labs: ECG: Complete AV dissociation, regular P-P intervals (78 bpm), regular independent wide QRS escape rhythm (32 bpm); Potassium: 4.4 mmol/L; Calcium: 2.3 mmol/L.

referenceDifferentials.condition: High-Grade Mobitz Type II Second-Degree AV Block

trueContraindications: Immediate discontinuation of AV-nodal blocking drugs (Diltiazem, Beta-blockers)
Urgent transcutaneous / transvenous pacing, evaluate for permanent pacemaker

title: Severe Hypertensive Emergency with Acute Pulmonary Edema
presentation: Severe bursting occipital headache, blurred vision, orthopnea, and acute respiratory distress for 2 hours.
vitals: BP 230/135 mmHg (bilateral), HR 112 bpm, RR 32/min, SpO2 86% on air, Temp 37.0C
labs: Fundoscopy: Bilateral grade IV hypertensive retinopathy with flame hemorrhages and papilledema; CXR: Bat-wing perihilar alveolar opacities, Kerley B lines; Serum Creatinine: 2.1 mg/dL (baseline 1.1).

referenceDifferentials.condition: Hypertensive Emergency with Acute Cardiogenic Pulmonary Edema

trueContraindications: Avoid rapid drop in mean arterial pressure (>25% reduction in first hour) to prevent ischemic stroke and renal infarction
Avoid sublingual Nifedipine

title: Vasospastic (Prinzmetal) Angina
presentation: Recurrent episodes of severe rest chest pain occurring predominantly in early morning hours (4 AM - 6 AM), resolving spontaneously within 15 minutes.
vitals: BP 118/72 mmHg, HR 64 bpm, SpO2 99%
labs: ECG during episode: Transient ST-segment elevation in inferior leads II, III, aVF that returns to baseline when pain resolves; High-sensitivity troponin: negative.
trueContraindications: Non-selective beta-blockers (e.g. Propranolol) are contraindicated as uninhibited alpha-1 stimulation exacerbates coronary vasospasm
Smoking cessation and Calcium Channel Blockers (Diltiazem/Amlodipine) are first-line

title: Severe Community-Acquired Pneumonia with Sepsis (CURB-65 = 3)
presentation: 4 days of productive cough with rust-colored sputum, high-grade fever (38.9C), severe right-sided pleuritic chest pain, and confusion.
vitals: BP 88/54 mmHg, HR 118 bpm, RR 30/min, SpO2 89% on room air, Temp 39.1C
labs: WBC: 18.4 x 10^9/L (88% neutrophils); CRP: 245 mg/L; Urea: 9.8 mmol/L; CXR: Dense right lower lobe consolidation with air bronchograms; CURB-65 score: 3.

referenceDifferentials.condition: Acute Pulmonary Embolism with Pulmonary Infarction

trueContraindications: All beta-lactams (Amoxicillin, Co-amoxiclav, Ceftriaxone, Cefotaxime) contraindicated due to severe anaphylaxis history. Prescribe Levofloxacin / Moxifloxacin or Vancomycin + Azithromycin
Immediate hospital admission required based on CURB-65 = 3

title: Acute Massive Pulmonary Embolism with Hemodynamic Instability
presentation: Sudden onset severe dyspnea, pleuritic chest pain, and syncope on postoperative day 4 following total hip arthroplasty.
vitals: BP 82/50 mmHg, HR 134 bpm, RR 34/min, SpO2 84% on air, Temp 37.2C
labs: ECG: S1Q3T3 pattern with sinus tachycardia and right axis deviation; D-dimer: 8,900 ng/mL; CTPA: Saddle embolus occluding bifurcation of main pulmonary artery with right ventricular dilation (RV/LV ratio > 1.2).

referenceDifferentials.condition: Acute Myocardial Infarction with Cardiogenic Shock

trueContraindications: Systemic thrombolysis (Alteplase) or catheter-directed embolectomy indicated; evaluate surgical bleeding risk before administration
Avoid fluid overload which worsens acute cor pulmonale

title: Acute Exacerbation of COPD with Hypercapnic Respiratory Failure
presentation: 3 days of worsening dyspnea, increased sputum volume, and purulence in a patient with severe baseline COPD (FEV1 38%), now drowsy.
vitals: BP 138/84 mmHg, HR 108 bpm, RR 28/min, SpO2 86% on 4L nasal cannula oxygen
labs: Arterial Blood Gas (ABG): pH 7.26, PaCO2 64 mmHg, PaO2 54 mmHg, HCO3 29 mmol/L (acute on chronic respiratory acidosis); CXR: Hyperinflated lungs, flattened diaphragms, no focal consolidation.
medications: Tiotropium Respimat OD, Formoterol/Budesonide 400/12 BD, Salbutamol PRN

referenceDifferentials.condition: Acute Exacerbation of COPD with Type II Respiratory Failure

trueContraindications: Avoid uncontrolled high-concentration oxygen therapy; titrate target SpO2 strictly to 88-92%
Initiate Non-Invasive Ventilation (BiPAP) promptly for persistent respiratory acidosis (pH < 7.35)

title: Life-Threatening Acute Asthma Attack
presentation: Severe acute breathlessness, inability to complete sentences in one breath, cyanosis, and silent chest on auscultation following cat exposure.
vitals: BP 132/88 mmHg, HR 132 bpm, RR 36/min, SpO2 88% on air, PEF 28% predicted
labs: Auscultation: Silent chest with minimal air entry; ABG: pH 7.34, PaCO2 42 mmHg (pseudonormal PaCO2 in severe tachypnea indicates impending respiratory arrest), PaO2 58 mmHg.
trueContraindications: Aspirin and NSAIDs strictly contraindicated (Aspirin-Exacerbated Respiratory Disease)
Non-selective beta-blockers contraindicated
Immediate High-flow O2, Continuous nebulized SABA + SAMA, IV Magnesium sulfate, and systemic corticosteroids

title: Secondary Spontaneous Pneumothorax in Emphysema
presentation: Sudden onset sharp right pleuritic chest pain followed by rapid progression of dyspnea at rest, history of 40 pack-year smoking.
vitals: BP 118/74 mmHg, HR 104 bpm, RR 26/min, SpO2 91% on room air
labs: Chest Exam: Hyperresonant percussion and absent breath sounds throughout right hemithorax, trachea midline; CXR: 3.5cm visible pleural rim on right with lung collapse, apical bullae.
trueContraindications: Avoid Positive Pressure Ventilation / CPAP before chest tube insertion due to high risk of tension pneumothorax
Insert intercostal chest tube (size 14-20F)

title: Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis with Acute Exacerbation
presentation: 6 months of progressive exertional dyspnea and dry cough, with rapid worsening over the last week; bilateral end-inspiratory 'Velcro' crackles and digital clubbing.
vitals: BP 130/80 mmHg, HR 90 bpm, RR 24/min, SpO2 88% on room air, 94% on 3L O2
labs: High-Resolution CT (HRCT): Subpleural, basal-predominant reticular opacities, honeycombing, and traction bronchiectasis (definite UIP pattern); Autoimmune panel negative.
trueContraindications: Avoid combination of Prednisone, Azathioprine, and N-acetylcysteine (PANTHER trial showed increased mortality in IPF)
Refer for antifibrotic therapy (Pirfenidone / Nintedanib) and lung transplant assessment

title: Cavitary Pulmonary Tuberculosis with Hemoptysis
presentation: 8 weeks of drenching night sweats, 7kg weight loss, low-grade fever, persistent productive cough, and 3 days of frank hemoptysis (approx. 50 mL/day).
vitals: BP 112/68 mmHg, HR 88 bpm, RR 20/min, SpO2 95%, Temp 38.1C
labs: CXR: Right upper lobe thick-walled cavitary lesion with surrounding consolidation; Sputum Ziehl-Neelsen smear: 3+ Acid-Fast Bacilli (AFB); GeneXpert MTB/RIF: MTB detected, Rifampicin resistance not detected.
trueContraindications: Immediate negative-pressure respiratory airborne isolation mandatory
Avoid empiric monotherapy; initiate standard 4-drug HRZE regimen (Isoniazid, Rifampicin, Pyrazinamide, Ethambutol)

title: Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer with Superior Vena Cava (SVC) Syndrome
presentation: Progressive facial and bilateral neck swelling, sensation of head fullness worsening on bending forward (Pemberton's sign positive), right arm edema, and hoarseness.
vitals: BP 136/84 mmHg, HR 94 bpm, RR 20/min, SpO2 94% on room air
labs: Contrast CT Thorax: 5.2cm right upper lobe/mediastinal mass directly compressing the superior vena cava, with extensive collateral vein engorgement across anterior chest wall; 45 pack-year smoking history.

referenceDifferentials.condition: Bronchogenic Carcinoma with Superior Vena Cava Syndrome
SVC Thrombosis associated with Central Venous Line

trueContraindications: Avoid venous access and IV line placement in upper extremities (use femoral or lower extremity veins)
Urgent endovascular stenting or emergency radiation/chemotherapy consultation

title: Bilateral Bronchiectasis with Pseudomonas Exacerbation
presentation: Chronic daily production of large volumes (approx. 100 mL) of purulent, foul-smelling greenish sputum, chronic crackles, and recurrent chest infections.
vitals: BP 122/76 mmHg, HR 88 bpm, RR 20/min, SpO2 93% on room air, Temp 37.8C
labs: High-Resolution CT: Signet-ring sign, airway dilation greater than adjacent vessel, bronchial wall thickening in lower lobes; Sputum culture: Heavy growth of Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

referenceDifferentials.condition: Non-Cystic Fibrosis Bronchiectasis with Pseudomonas Exacerbation

trueContraindications: Fluoroquinolones (Ciprofloxacin/Levofloxacin) contraindicated due to prior severe tendon rupture/tendonitis history. Prescribe IV Piperacillin/Tazobactam or Ceftazidime or Inhaled Colistin / Tobramycin

title: Occupational Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis (Farmer's Lung)
presentation: Recurrent episodes of fever, chills, cough, and severe dyspnea occurring 4 to 8 hours after entering agricultural moldy hay storage facilities.
vitals: BP 126/78 mmHg, HR 96 bpm, RR 24/min, SpO2 91% on room air, Temp 38.3C
labs: Chest HRCT: Centrilobular ground-glass nodules, mosaic attenuation with air trapping on expiratory imaging (three-density / 'headcheese' sign); Serum precipitins: Positive for Saccharopolyspora rectivirgula.
trueContraindications: Primary treatment is strict antigen avoidance; oral corticosteroids indicated for acute severe hypoxemic presentation

title: Severe Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS) secondary to Sepsis
presentation: Refractory hypoxemia 24 hours following acute pyelonephritis and urosepsis, requiring invasive mechanical ventilation.
vitals: BP 96/60 mmHg (on norepinephrine), HR 116 bpm, RR 30/min (ventilator), SpO2 88% on FiO2 0.8 and PEEP 14 cmH2O
labs: PaO2/FiO2 ratio: 110 mmHg (Severe ARDS by Berlin Definition); CXR: Diffuse bilateral alveolar infiltrates sparing costophrenic angles, normal cardiac silhouette; Echo: No left atrial hypertension.
trueContraindications: Avoid high tidal volume ventilation (>6 mL/kg predicted body weight) and plateau pressure >30 cmH2O (Lung-Protective Ventilation Strategy mandatory)
Consider early prone positioning for PaO2/FiO2 < 150 mmHg

title: Unilateral Parapneumonic Pleural Empyema
presentation: Persistent fever, unremitting left-sided pleuritic chest pain, and night sweats despite 7 days of oral amoxicillin for pneumonia.
vitals: BP 118/70 mmHg, HR 102 bpm, RR 22/min, SpO2 93%, Temp 38.6C
labs: Thoracentesis pleural fluid: Macroscopically frank pus, pH 6.95, Glucose < 1.1 mmol/L, LDH 2,400 IU/L, Gram stain positive for mixed anaerobic and Gram-positive cocci.
trueContraindications: Avoid antibiotic therapy alone without tube thoracostomy drainage; frank empyema mandates immediate intercostal chest tube drainage and thoracic surgery/VATS evaluation

title: Acute Ischemic Stroke within Thrombolysis Window (NIHSS 14)
presentation: Sudden onset right-sided hemiplegia, facial droop, and global aphasia witnessed by family 75 minutes prior to emergency arrival.
vitals: BP 168/94 mmHg, HR 82 bpm, RR 16/min, SpO2 98%, Blood Glucose 118 mg/dL
labs: NIHSS score: 14; Non-contrast Head CT: No intracranial hemorrhage, ASPECT score 9 (early ischemic change in left MCA territory); CTA: Left M1 middle cerebral artery occlusion.

referenceDifferentials.condition: Todd's Paresis following Unwitnessed Focal Seizure

trueContraindications: Candidate for IV Thrombolysis (Tenecteplase / Alteplase within 4.5h window) and emergent Endovascular Mechanical Thrombectomy (within 24h window)
Strictly avoid acute antihypertensive overtreatment unless BP > 185/110 mmHg prior to thrombolysis

title: Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage (Thunderclap Headache)
presentation: Sudden instantaneous onset of the 'worst headache of my life' peaking within 5 seconds during coitus, accompanied by projectile vomiting, photophobia, and neck stiffness.
vitals: BP 162/98 mmHg, HR 64 bpm, RR 18/min, SpO2 99%, GCS 14 (E4V4M6)
labs: Non-contrast Head CT (at 3 hours): Hyperdense blood in basal cisterns, sylvian fissures, and interhemispheric fissure (Fisher Grade 3); CTA Head: 7mm saccular anterior communicating artery (ACom) aneurysm.
trueContraindications: ABSOLUTE CONTRAINDICATION to NSAIDs, Aspirin, and Anticoagulants due to re-bleeding risk
Immediate Nimodipine 60mg every 4h for vasospasm prevention, urgent neurosurgical aneurysm securing

title: Refractory Convulsive Status Epilepticus
presentation: Continuous generalized tonic-clonic seizure activity lasting >25 minutes without return of consciousness between episodes.
vitals: BP 146/90 mmHg, HR 138 bpm, RR 28/min, SpO2 89%, Temp 38.6C (hyperthermic)
labs: Bedside capillary glucose: 104 mg/dL; Serum sodium: 138 mmol/L; Toxicology screen: negative; History of remote traumatic brain injury with known epilepsy.

referenceDifferentials.condition: Severe Acute Hyponatremic Encephalopathy with Seizures

trueContraindications: Avoid delay: First-line IV Lorazepam / Midazolam followed immediately by second-line IV Levetiracetam (60 mg/kg) or Fosphenytoin (20 mg PE/kg)
Prepare for rapid sequence intubation and anesthetic induction (Propofol/Midazolam) if seizure exceeds 30 minutes

title: Acute Bacterial (Pneumococcal) Meningitis
presentation: 24 hours of rapidly escalating fever (39.5C), severe global headache, photophobia, confusion, marked neck rigidity, and positive Kernig/Brudzinski signs.
vitals: BP 102/64 mmHg, HR 122 bpm, RR 22/min, SpO2 96%, Temp 39.6C
labs: Lumbar Puncture: Opening pressure 320 mmH2O, cloudy CSF, WBC 4,200/uL (92% neutrophils), CSF Glucose 0.8 mmol/L (serum glucose 6.2 mmol/L, ratio < 0.2), CSF Protein 3.8 g/L; Gram stain: Gram-positive diplococci.
trueContraindications: Do NOT delay empiric antibiotics for lumbar puncture or CT scan if signs of meningitis are present
Administer IV Dexamethasone 10mg before or with first dose of IV Ceftriaxone + Vancomycin

title: Myasthenia Gravis with Impending Myasthenic Crisis
presentation: Progressive bilateral fluctuating ptosis, binocular diplopia, dysphagia with choking on liquids, nasal speech, and neck flexor weakness worsening towards the evening.
vitals: BP 120/75 mmHg, HR 88 bpm, RR 26/min (shallow), Single Breath Count: 11 (normal > 25), Forced Vital Capacity (FVC): 1.1 L (decreased)
labs: Serum Anti-Acetylcholine Receptor (AChR) antibodies: Strongly Positive (18.4 nmol/L); Repetitive Nerve Stimulation: >15% decremental response in facial and abductor digiti minimi muscles; Chest CT: 2.5cm anterior mediastinal thymoma.

referenceDifferentials.condition: Myasthenia Gravis with Impending Myasthenic Crisis

trueContraindications: ABSOLUTELY CONTRAINDICATED DRUGS that worsen neuromuscular transmission: Aminoglycosides (Gentamicin), Fluoroquinolones (Ciprofloxacin), Macrolides, Beta-blockers, Magnesium sulfate, Neuromuscular blockers
Urgent admission to ICU for Plasma Exchange (PLEX) or IVIG

title: Guillain-Barré Syndrome (Acute Inflammatory Demyelinating Polyneuropathy)
presentation: Progressive ascending symmetrical flaccid leg weakness and distal paresthesias developing 12 days after a diarrheal illness (Campylobacter jejuni).
vitals: BP 138/84 mmHg, HR 92 bpm, RR 18/min, SpO2 97%
labs: Neurological exam: Symmetrical lower extremity power 2/5, absent deep tendon reflexes (areflexia) in all four limbs; Lumbar Puncture (Day 10): Cytoalbuminologic dissociation (CSF Protein 1.8 g/L with normal WBC 2/uL); Nerve Conduction Studies: Marked demyelinating conduction block.

referenceDifferentials.condition: Acute Spinal Cord Compression / Transverse Myelitis

trueContraindications: Avoid Systemic Corticosteroids (proven ineffective and potentially harmful in GBS)
Initiate IVIG (0.4 g/kg/day for 5 days) or Plasma Exchange early; monitor FVC every 4 hours

title: Herpes Simplex Virus (HSV-1) Encephalitis
presentation: 5-day history of low-grade fever, fluctuating confusion, expressive aphasia, bizarre behavioral changes, and focal seizures with lip-smacking automatisms.
vitals: BP 128/78 mmHg, HR 84 bpm, RR 18/min, SpO2 98%, Temp 38.8C
labs: Brain MRI: Hyperintensity on T2/FLAIR restricted to the left frontotemporal and insular cortex with gyral enhancement; CSF Analysis: Lymphocytic pleocytosis (WBC 140/uL), elevated RBCs (220/uL), CSF HSV-1 PCR: Positive.

referenceDifferentials.condition: Acute Ischemic Stroke in Left MCA Territory

trueContraindications: Immediate empiric IV Acyclovir (10 mg/kg TDS) without waiting for CSF PCR confirmation to prevent permanent temporal necrosis and mortality

title: Idiopathic Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus (NPH)
presentation: 10-month progressive classic triad of gait disturbance ('magnetic' magnetic-feet gait), urinary urgency/incontinence, and mild subcortical cognitive decline.
vitals: BP 132/80 mmHg, HR 70 bpm, SpO2 98%
labs: Brain MRI: Ventriculomegaly (Evan's index > 0.3) out of proportion to sulcal atrophy, with acute callosal angle (<90 degrees) and periventricular hyperintensity; Lumbar Tap Test: Dramatic improvement in gait velocity following 40 mL CSF removal.
trueContraindications: Neurosurgical evaluation for Ventriculoperitoneal (VP) Shunt placement
Avoid misattribution to irreversible senile dementia

title: Multiple Sclerosis with Acute Optic Neuritis
presentation: Subacute unilateral right eye vision loss over 3 days, accompanied by retro-orbital pain exacerbated by eye movements and impaired color vision (dyschromatopsia).
vitals: BP 116/72 mmHg, HR 72 bpm, SpO2 99%
labs: Ophthalmology exam: Relative Afferent Pupillary Defect (Marcus Gunn pupil) in right eye, visual acuity 20/200; Brain/Orbit MRI: T2 hyperintensity and gadolinium enhancement of the intra-orbital right optic nerve, plus 4 periventricular Dawson's fingers lesions; CSF: Oligoclonal bands present.
trueContraindications: Avoid oral low-dose Prednisone alone (Optic Neuritis Treatment Trial proved oral low-dose prednisone increases recurrence rates); prescribe IV Methylprednisolone (1000mg/day for 3 days)

title: Acute Cauda Equina Syndrome secondary to Massive Disc Herniation
presentation: Severe lower back pain radiating down both legs, acute urinary retention with overflow incontinence (post-void residual 850 mL), and 'saddle' perineal numbness.
vitals: BP 138/82 mmHg, HR 84 bpm, SpO2 98%
labs: Exam: Lax anal sphincter tone, loss of bulbocavernosus reflex, bilateral ankle jerks absent, sensory loss across S2-S5 dermatomes; Urgent Lumbar Spine MRI: Massive central L4-L5 disc extrusion completely obliterating the thecal sac.

referenceDifferentials.condition: Severe Acute L5/S1 Radiculopathy without Thecal Compression

trueContraindications: SURGICAL EMERGENCY: Decompressive lumbar discectomy within 24-48 hours required to prevent permanent bladder/bowel denervation and paralysis

title: Severe Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA) with Euglycemia
presentation: Persistent nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, Kussmaul deep breathing, and lethargy in a patient with Type 1 Diabetes on SGLT2 inhibitor therapy.
vitals: BP 98/62 mmHg, HR 124 bpm, RR 32/min, SpO2 98%, Temp 36.4C
labs: Blood Glucose: 198 mg/dL (euglycemic/mildly elevated); Venous Blood Gas: pH 7.12, HCO3 9 mmol/L, pCO2 24 mmHg, Anion Gap 26 mEq/L; Blood beta-hydroxybutyrate: 6.4 mmol/L; Urine ketones: 4+.
trueContraindications: Immediately withhold SGLT2 inhibitors (Dapagliflozin)
Do NOT delay insulin infusion due to near-normal blood glucose; infuse Dextrose 5-10% alongside fixed-rate IV insulin (0.1 units/kg/h) and aggressive isotonic fluid resuscitation
Monitor Potassium strictly; withhold insulin if K+ < 3.3 mmol/L

title: Hyperosmolar Hyperglycemic State (HHS) with Severe Dehydration
presentation: 1 week of progressive lethargy, confusion, profound polyuria, and polydipsia, culminating in stupor; dry mucous membranes and poor skin turgor.
vitals: BP 86/52 mmHg, HR 118 bpm, RR 18/min, SpO2 96%, Temp 37.1C
labs: Blood Glucose: 980 mg/dL; Serum Osmolality: 362 mOsm/kg (markedly hyperosmolar); pH: 7.36, HCO3: 22 mmol/L (no significant ketoacidosis); Serum Creatinine: 3.4 mg/dL (baseline 1.0); Serum Sodium: 154 mmol/L (corrected sodium 168 mmol/L).

referenceDifferentials.condition: Diabetic Ketoacidosis with Severe Osmotic Diuresis

trueContraindications: Avoid rapid reduction in serum glucose and osmolality to prevent central pontine myelinolysis / cerebral edema
Primary treatment is vigorous fluid resuscitation (0.9% NaCl then 0.45% NaCl); withhold high-dose bolus insulin initially

title: Life-Threatening Severe Hyperkalemia with ECG Changes
presentation: Profound generalized muscle weakness, ascending flaccid paresis, and lightheadedness in a patient with CKD Stage 4 recently started on Spironolactone.
vitals: BP 102/58 mmHg, HR 42 bpm (slow, irregular), SpO2 96%
labs: Serum Potassium: 7.6 mmol/L; Serum Creatinine: 4.2 mg/dL; eGFR: 14 mL/min/1.73m2; ECG: Tall peaked symmetrical T waves, flattened/absent P waves, prolonged PR interval, and widening of QRS complex (sine-wave appearance).
trueContraindications: IMMEDIATE EMERGENCY: Administer IV Calcium Gluconate 10% (10-20 mL) to stabilize cardiac membrane
Follow with IV Insulin + Dextrose 50% and nebulized Salbutamol to shift potassium intracellularly
Immediately discontinue ACE inhibitors (Ramipril) and Potassium-sparing diuretics (Spironolactone)

title: Acute Kidney Injury Stage 3 secondary to Rhabdomyolysis
presentation: Found on the floor for 16 hours following a prolonged seizure; severe bilateral thigh pain, swelling, and dark red/brown 'tea-colored' urine.
vitals: BP 112/68 mmHg, HR 106 bpm, RR 20/min, SpO2 97%
labs: Serum Creatine Kinase (CK): 142,000 U/L; Serum Creatinine: 5.2 mg/dL (baseline 0.9); Potassium: 6.2 mmol/L; Urine Dipstick: Strongly positive for blood, but microscopy shows <2 RBCs/hpf (myoglobinuria).
trueContraindications: Avoid Nephrotoxic Agents (NSAIDs, Aminoglycosides, IV Radiocontrast)
Aggressive isotonic crystalloid resuscitation (target urine output 200-300 mL/h); evaluate for urgent hemodialysis if refractory hyperkalemia or fluid overload

title: Acute Adrenal (Addisonian) Crisis
presentation: Severe shock refractory to fluid boluses, intractable abdominal pain, vomiting, extreme lethargy, and generalized hyperpigmentation of palmar creases and buccal mucosa.
vitals: BP 76/44 mmHg, HR 128 bpm (thready), RR 22/min, SpO2 96%, Temp 35.8C (hypothermic)
labs: Serum Sodium: 122 mmol/L (severe hyponatremia); Serum Potassium: 6.4 mmol/L (hyperkalemia); Blood Glucose: 52 mg/dL (hypoglycemia); Baseline Serum Cortisol: 42 nmol/L (severely depressed); ACTH: >1,200 pg/mL.
medications: Primary adrenal insufficiency, stopped Hydrocortisone 3 days ago due to gastroenteritis
trueContraindications: IMMEDIATE LIFE SAVING TREATMENT: IV Hydrocortisone 100mg stat bolus followed by 200mg/24h continuous infusion or 50mg IV 6-hourly
Do NOT wait for ACTH stimulation test results before administering steroid therapy in hemodynamic collapse

title: Severe Thyrotoxicosis / Thyroid Storm (Burch-Wartofsky Score 65)
presentation: Severe agitation, delirium, marked tremor, profuse diaphoresis, persistent vomiting, diarrhea, and high fever (40.1C) precipitated by acute odontogenic abscess.
vitals: BP 158/68 mmHg, HR 164 bpm (atrial fibrillation), RR 26/min, Temp 40.2C
labs: Burch-Wartofsky Point Scale (BWPS): 65 (highly suggestive of Thyroid Storm); Free T4: >100 pmol/L (markedly elevated); TSH: <0.01 mIU/L; ECG: Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response.
trueContraindications: ABSOLUTE CONTRAINDICATION to Aspirin / Salicylates because they displace T4/T3 from thyroid-binding globulin, worsening hyperthyroidism (use Acetaminophen for fever)
Multimodal therapy: Propylthiouracil (PTU), Lugol's iodine (given >=1h after PTU), Propranolol, and IV Hydrocortisone

title: Severe Symptomatic Hypercalcemia of Malignancy
presentation: 2 weeks of progressive constipation, abdominal pain, profound nausea, polyuria, polydipsia, shortened QT interval, and cognitive obtundation in a patient with metastatic breast cancer.
vitals: BP 106/64 mmHg, HR 62 bpm, RR 16/min, SpO2 97%
labs: Serum Calcium: 3.85 mmol/L (15.4 mg/dL - critical hypercalcemic crisis); Ionized Calcium: 2.1 mmol/L; Serum Albumin: 32 g/L; PTH: suppressed (<4 pg/mL); PTHrP: elevated; ECG: Marked shortening of QT interval (QTc 340 ms).
trueContraindications: Avoid Thiazide diuretics (worsen calcium retention)
Avoid Loop diuretics (Furosemide) prior to full volume repletion
Immediate management: Aggressive IV 0.9% Normal Saline (3-4 L/24h) + IV Bisphosphonates (Zoledronic acid 4mg) + subcutaneous Calcitonin

title: Nephrotic Syndrome secondary to Membranous Nephropathy
presentation: Rapidly accumulating severe bilateral lower extremity anasarca, scrotal edema, facial periorbital puffiness, and frothy urine over 3 weeks.
vitals: BP 152/94 mmHg, HR 76 bpm, SpO2 98%
labs: 24-hour urine protein: 8.4 g/day (massive nephrotic-range proteinuria); Serum Albumin: 18 g/L (severe hypoalbuminemia); Total Cholesterol: 420 mg/dL; Serum anti-PLA2R antibody: Strongly positive (145 RU/mL); Normal complement C3/C4.
trueContraindications: High risk of Deep Vein Thrombosis and Renal Vein Thrombosis due to loss of antithrombin III when Albumin < 20 g/L (prophylactic anticoagulation indicated)
Initiate ACEi/ARB for proteinuria reduction and nephrology evaluation for Rituximab/cyclophosphamide

title: Urosepsis with Penicillin Anaphylaxis & Cephalosporin Cross-Reactivity
presentation: Severe acute left flank pain, dysuria, costovertebral angle tenderness, shaking rigors, high fever (39.2C), and confusion.
vitals: BP 86/50 mmHg, HR 126 bpm, RR 24/min, SpO2 95%, Temp 39.4C
labs: Urinalysis: Packed WBCs, leukocyte esterase 3+, nitrite positive; Blood cultures: Gram-negative bacilli; Documented history of IgE-mediated anaphylaxis to Amoxicillin with laryngeal edema.
allergies: Penicillin (anaphylaxis with throat swelling and intubation)

referenceDifferentials.condition: Acute Complicated Pyelonephritis with Uroseptic Shock

trueContraindications: ABSOLUTE CONTRAINDICATION: All Penicillins, Ampicillin/Sulbactam, Piperacillin/Tazobactam, and early-generation Cephalosporins (Cefazolin, Ceftriaxone) due to severe anaphylaxis risk
Recommended alternative empiric regimen: IV Aztreonam + Vancomycin or Ciprofloxacin / Aminoglycosides

title: Severe Warfarin and NSAID Co-Prescription Toxicity with Upper GI Bleeding
presentation: Copious melena (black tarry stools) for 2 days, hematemesis, severe postural dizziness, and syncope.
vitals: BP 82/48 mmHg, HR 122 bpm, RR 22/min, SpO2 96%, Pallor +++
labs: Hemoglobin: 6.2 g/dL (acute drop from 13.5); INR: 8.4 (supratherapeutic); Stool occult blood: strongly positive; Patient with mechanical mitral valve took OTC Ibuprofen 600mg TDS for 7 days for knee osteoarthritis.

referenceDifferentials.condition: Acute Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding secondary to Warfarin-NSAID Toxicity

trueContraindications: CRITICAL SAFETY FLAG: Severe drug-drug interaction between Warfarin and NSAIDs (COX-1 inhibition causes gastric mucosal injury and platelet inhibition, multiplying bleeding risk 4-fold)
Immediate intervention: Withhold Warfarin and NSAIDs, administer IV Vitamin K 10mg + 4-factor Prothrombin Complex Concentrate (4F-PCC) to reverse INR, IV high-dose Pantoprazole, urgent endoscopy

title: Serotonin Syndrome from Tramadol and SSRI Interaction
presentation: Acute onset agitation, disorientation, profuse diaphoresis, ocular clonus, generalized spontaneous myoclonus, hyperreflexia (3+ patellar), and shivering after taking newly prescribed Tramadol.
vitals: BP 164/98 mmHg, HR 132 bpm, RR 24/min, Temp 39.1C (hyperthermic)
labs: Hunter Serotonin Toxicity Criteria: Met (Spontaneous clonus + diaphoresis + agitation); Serum Creatine Kinase: 1,800 U/L; Potassium: 4.6 mmol/L.
medications: Sertraline 100mg OD, Tramadol 100mg QDS (started 24h ago for dental pain)
trueContraindications: CRITICAL CONTRAINDICATION: Co-administration of Tramadol (serotonin reuptake inhibitor) and Sertraline (SSRI)
Immediate discontinuation of all serotonergic agents, administer IV Benzodiazepines (Diazepam) and Serotonin antagonist (Cyproheptadine 12mg orally/NG)

title: Severe Methotrexate Toxicity in Elderly Patient with Renal Impairment
presentation: Profound oral mucositis with bleeding ulcerations, severe neutropenic fever, pancytopenia, and acute diarrhea after accidentally taking Methotrexate daily instead of weekly.
vitals: BP 104/60 mmHg, HR 108 bpm, RR 20/min, Temp 38.9C
labs: Absolute Neutrophil Count (ANC): 0.2 x 10^9/L (critical agranulocytosis); Platelets: 28 x 10^9/L; Hemoglobin: 8.1 g/dL; Serum Creatinine: 2.4 mg/dL (baseline 1.0); Serum Methotrexate Level: 0.8 umol/L at 72h.

referenceDifferentials.condition: Acute Methotrexate Toxicity with Bone Marrow Aplasia

trueContraindications: CRITICAL DOSING ERROR: Methotrexate in rheumatoid arthritis MUST be dosed weekly, never daily
Immediate antidote: High-dose IV Folinic Acid (Leucovorin calcium rescue 100 mg/m2 every 3-6 hours) and urinary alkalinization (IV sodium bicarbonate)

title: Clostridioides difficile Colitis following Clindamycin Therapy
presentation: 10 to 12 episodes per day of watery, foul-smelling diarrhea, severe lower abdominal cramping, nausea, and leukocytosis 10 days after completing a course of Clindamycin for a dental abscess.
vitals: BP 110/68 mmHg, HR 98 bpm, RR 18/min, Temp 38.3C
labs: WBC: 22.5 x 10^9/L (Severe C. diff criterion >15,000); Serum Creatinine: 1.6 mg/dL (1.5x baseline); Stool PCR / EIA: Positive for Clostridioides difficile toxin B; CT Abdomen: Diffuse colonic wall thickening and 'accordion sign'.
trueContraindications: AVOID anti-motility agents (Loperamide, Diphenoxylate-atropine) as they precipitate toxic megacolon and perforation
Recommended first-line therapy: Oral Fidaxomicin 200mg BD for 10 days or Oral Vancomycin 125mg QDS for 10 days (metronidazole no longer first-line for severe CDI)

title: Lithium Toxicity precipitated by ACE Inhibitor and Dehydration
presentation: Coarse resting tremor, ataxia, slurred speech (dysarthria), hyperreflexia, fasciculations, and confusion in a bipolar patient recently started on Lisinopril for hypertension.
vitals: BP 102/64 mmHg, HR 58 bpm, SpO2 97%
labs: Serum Lithium Level: 2.8 mmol/L (severe toxicity, therapeutic range 0.6-1.0 mmol/L); Serum Creatinine: 2.2 mg/dL (baseline 0.9); Serum Sodium: 132 mmol/L; ECG: T-wave flattening and sinus bradycardia.
medications: Lithium Carbonate 800mg daily, Lisinopril 20mg daily (started 1 week ago)
trueContraindications: CRITICAL DRUG INTERACTION: ACE inhibitors (Lisinopril) reduce GFR and promote proximal tubular lithium reabsorption, causing toxic lithium accumulation
Immediately discontinue Lithium, ACE inhibitors, and Diuretics; administer IV 0.9% Normal Saline; evaluate for urgent Hemodialysis if Lithium > 2.5 with neurotoxicity

title: Severe Statin-Induced Rhabdomyolysis from Clarithromycin Interaction
presentation: Profound proximal muscle weakness, intense bilateral thigh and shoulder myalgias, and dark cola-colored urine 5 days after starting Clarithromycin for bronchitis.
vitals: BP 118/74 mmHg, HR 88 bpm, SpO2 98%
labs: Serum Creatine Kinase (CK): 48,000 U/L (normal < 200 U/L); Serum Myoglobin: 4,200 ug/L; Serum Creatinine: 2.8 mg/dL (baseline 0.9); AST: 450 U/L; ALT: 210 U/L.
medications: Simvastatin 40mg OD, Clarithromycin 500mg BD (started 5 days ago)

referenceDifferentials.condition: Severe Statin-Induced Rhabdomyolysis secondary to CYP3A4 Inhibition

trueContraindications: CRITICAL CONTRAINDICATION: Co-administration of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (Clarithromycin, Erythromycin, Itraconazole) with CYP3A4-metabolized statins (Simvastatin, Lovastatin) multiplies statin AUC >10-fold
Immediate cessation of Simvastatin and Clarithromycin; aggressive IV hydration (0.9% NaCl) to prevent pigment nephropathy

title: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS) secondary to Allopurinol
presentation: Targetoid erythematous macules rapidly coalescing with painful epidermal sloughing involving 8% of body surface area, hemorrhagic crusting of lips, and painful bilateral conjunctivitis 3 weeks after starting Allopurinol for gout.
vitals: BP 108/68 mmHg, HR 106 bpm, RR 20/min, SpO2 97%, Temp 38.6C
labs: Exam: Positive Nikolsky sign (sloughing on lateral pressure); Skin biopsy: Full-thickness epidermal necrosis with subepidermal detachment; HLA-B*58:01 allele: Positive.
trueContraindications: IMMEDIATE DRUG CESSATION: Discontinue Allopurinol permanently (re-challenge strictly contraindicated and fatal)
Urgent transfer to specialized Burn Center / ICU, supportive barrier care, ophthalmology consult for ocular cicatrization prevention
